blogs.title: Getting Started with React Hooks
blogs.summary: A comprehensive guide to understanding and using React Hooks in modern development
blogs.content:
React Hooks have revolutionized the way we write React components. In this comprehensive guide, we'll explore:

## Introduction to Hooks
Hooks are functions that let you hook into React features. They allow you to use state and other React features without writing class components.

## Common Hooks

### useState
Manages component state in functional components.

### useEffect
Handles side effects like API calls, subscriptions, and DOM manipulations.

### useContext
Access context values without deeply nested consumers.

## Custom Hooks
Create reusable logic by writing your own custom hooks that abstract away complex state and side effect logic.

## Best Practices
- Only call hooks at the top level
- Only call hooks from React functions
- Use the ESLint plugin to enforce these rules

Mastering hooks will significantly improve your React development skills and code quality.

blogs.title: Web Performance Optimization Tips
blogs.summary: Essential techniques to improve your website's loading speed and performance
blogs.content:
Website performance is crucial for user experience and SEO rankings. Here are essential optimization techniques:

## Image Optimization
- Use WebP format for modern browsers
- Implement lazy loading for below-the-fold images
- Use responsive images with srcset
- Compress images without losing quality

## Code Splitting
- Split JavaScript bundles by route
- Load only necessary code per page
- Use dynamic imports for conditional loading

## Caching Strategies
- Implement browser caching with proper headers
- Use service workers for offline support
- Cache API responses intelligently

## CSS Optimization
- Minify and compress CSS files
- Remove unused CSS with tools like PurgeCSS
- Inline critical CSS
- Use CSS Grid and Flexbox for layouts

## Monitoring
- Use Chrome DevTools for profiling
- Monitor Core Web Vitals
- Set up performance budgets

Optimizing performance can increase conversion rates by up to 7% per second of improvement.

blogs.title: Understanding Node.js Event Loop
blogs.summary: Deep dive into how Node.js handles asynchronous operations
blogs.content:
The Event Loop is the heart of Node.js asynchronous programming. Understanding it is crucial for writing efficient server-side code.

## What is the Event Loop?
The Event Loop is a mechanism that allows Node.js to perform non-blocking I/O operations despite JavaScript being single-threaded.

## Phases of Event Loop

### 1. Timers
Executes callbacks scheduled by setTimeout() and setInterval().

### 2. Pending Callbacks
Executes deferred I/O callbacks.

### 3. Idle, Prepare
Internal use only.

### 4. Poll
Retrieve new I/O events. Execute callbacks.

### 5. Check
Executes setImmediate() callbacks.

### 6. Close Callbacks
Execute close callbacks.

## Microtasks vs Macrotasks
- Microtasks: Promises, process.nextTick()
- Macrotasks: setTimeout, setInterval

Microtasks always run before the next macrotask, which is important for understanding callback execution order.

## Best Practices
- Avoid blocking the event loop with long-running operations
- Use async/await for cleaner asynchronous code
- Monitor event loop lag in production

Mastering the event loop will help you write high-performance Node.js applications.

blogs.title: CSS Grid vs Flexbox - When to Use Each
blogs.summary: A practical comparison of CSS layout methods and their best use cases
blogs.content:
CSS Grid and Flexbox are powerful layout tools, but they serve different purposes. Let's explore when to use each.

## Flexbox Overview
Flexbox is a one-dimensional layout method for arranging items in rows or columns.

### Best for:
- Navigation bars
- Card layouts in a single row/column
- Centering content
- Simple linear layouts

### Advantages:
- Simpler syntax for 1D layouts
- Better browser support (IE 10+)
- Excellent for alignment and spacing

## CSS Grid Overview
CSS Grid is a two-dimensional layout method for creating complex grid layouts.

### Best for:
- Page layouts
- Complex multi-column designs
- Responsive grid systems
- Overlapping layouts

### Advantages:
- Perfect for 2D layouts
- Great for responsive design
- More control over item placement

## Practical Examples

### Use Flexbox for:
```css
.navbar { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; }
```

### Use Grid for:
```css
.layout { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 2fr 1fr; }
```

## Combining Both
You can combine Grid and Flexbox in the same layout. Use Grid for major page structure and Flexbox for component-level alignment.
